statement: Let a be a nondecreasing rearrangement of nums, so a has length n, a[0] <= a[1] <= ... <= a[n-1], and a is a permutation of nums. The function returns a result r and r = min(a[n-1] - a[2], a[n-2] - a[1], a[n-3] - a[0]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r; in particular, under these preconditions it does not fail, panic, encounter integer overflow, or access an out-of-bounds index.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= (max over 0 <= i < n of nums[i]) - (min over 0 <= i < n of nums[i]).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let a be a nondecreasing rearrangement of nums. Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= a[n-1] - a[2], r <= a[n-2] - a[1], and r <= a[n-3] - a[0].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there exists an integer v such that the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n and nums[i] = v is at least n - 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns results r on nums and r2 on nums2, and r2 = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000. Let nums2 be any list of length n that is a permutation of nums.

statement: The function returns results r on nums and r_shifted on shifted, and r_shifted = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000. Let c be an integer such that 1 <= nums[i] + c <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. Let shifted be the list of length n with shifted[i] = nums[i] + c.

statement: The function returns results r on nums and r_scaled on scaled, and r_scaled = c * r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000. Let c be a positive integer such that 1 <= c * nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. Let scaled be the list of length n with scaled[i] = c * nums[i].

statement: The function returns results r on nums and r_reflected on reflected, and r_reflected = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000. Let C be an integer such that 1 <= C - nums[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. Let reflected be the list of length n with reflected[i] = C - nums[i].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist an array b of length n and a set I of at most two indices such that: (i) b[i] = nums[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n and i not in I; (ii) the score of b, defined as (max over 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n of |b[i] - b[j]|) + (min over 0 <= i < j < n of |b[i] - b[j]|), is equal to r; and (iii) min over 0 <= i < j < n of |b[i] - b[j]| = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every array b of length n and every set I of at most two indices such that b[i] = nums[i] for all i with 0 <= i < n and i not in I, the score of b, defined as (max over 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n of |b[i] - b[j]|) + (min over 0 <= i < j < n of |b[i] - b[j]|), is at least r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: If a[i] = a2[i] for every i in the set containing 0, 1, 2, n-3, n-2, and n-1, then the function returns results r on nums and r2 on nums2, and r2 = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 3 <= n <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000. Let nums2 be another list of length n satisfying the same bounds. Let a and a2 be nondecreasing rearrangements of nums and nums2 respectively.
